FIVE INDEPENDENT WORLDS

NIGHTGLASS COURIER

The Door We Haven’t Seen

A pickup request has a time, but no one has walked the door. An honest refusal and one limited working trial may find a promise that fits.

Next morning. Tenth round complete.

They will still be there when you have put your money away.

I have the request. I still do not know the door.

SERA
Then we look before we promise.

Stay on the dry side, please.

You asked about first-bell collection. This is Aren, and Sera came to see the approach.

EDDA
First bell is when this doorway is clear.

Second bell.

The tubs keep moving through second bell. I cannot stop the wash floor for a cart.

First bell is my Lower Post round. I cannot take that time.

Then why did you come?

AREN
Because we had not looked at the door.

EDDA
Good. Look before you quote me.

These are ours. Two small bundles, dry and tied. We can try with them.
end_text:
e load is going before you put my cart in the plan.

AREN
Door, load and your hours. Then a price.

Dry hatch. Two bundles. One forecourt trial.

SERA
That is what we have seen.

For your time. The stopped attempt counted too.

And yours.

Next time, knock here before you bring anything.

AREN
We will ask about the load first.

I nearly said first bell just to keep her listening.

DARO
She listened when you stopped guessing about her morning.

I have my next job. Ask me before you accept the next load.

AREN
I will.

You stopped the first method before it stopped her work.

AREN
I still want to take the route assessment I missed.

SERA
Ask for the hours and the load. I can say what I saw; the assessor decides what is tested.

AREN
Tomorrow after the post. I ask before I commit.

I want to know which part I am ready for.

SERA
Then that is the question we take.

End of Chapter 8
